transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-04-27
- Start: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Product), Samir (Holloway CTO), Ruth (Holloway VP Product), Leo (Cloud Infra), Asha (Security)

Summary: quick kickoff for a marketplace listing + joint pilot. Primary goals: confirm networking/KMS constraints for Holloway regulated workloads, agree on pilot success metrics (p95 latency, cost per 1K tokens, throughput), and schedule a deploy lab to validate helm/installer and telemetry. Customer expressed preference for private listing via cloud marketplace and an on-prem option later.

Links referenced: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/marketplace-onramp (shared), pilot spreadsheet: https://drive.company/holloway-pilot-v1.xlsx

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick agenda - marketplace listing checklist, network/KMS questions, pilot metrics and timeline, and a hands-on deploy lab. if we run over we can follow up.
[00:28] Samir Patel: thanks maya, yep excited. quick intro from our side - i'm samir cto, ruth runs product and leo is infra. we have a few regs so the KMS and vpc pieces are, like, gating.
[00:47] Diego Alvarez: hi all, diego here, i will be the se on the deployment side. i wanted to flag early on that the marketplace listing on azure has a couple of required artifacts - installer or helm chart, edge/csi packaging, and an arm template if you want native marketplace deploy.
[01:12] Ruth Ng: can you say more about the arm template bit? our infra team prefers template-driven provisioning to manage identity and network.
[01:25] Diego Alvarez: yeah absolutely. the template basically wires up the service principals, vnet peering if needed, and supports parameters for customer-managed keys. it's not mandatory but it smooths the installer experience and allows one-click marketplace provisioning. sometimes the transcribed notes show it as "a-r-m" or "arm" templates, sorry i mean ARM template.
[01:50] Asha Kapoor: from security, we need details on key rotation and HSM support. do you support bring-your-own-kms or HSM-backed keys?
[02:05] Priya Nair: short answer: yes. Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and HSM via customer KMS providers; the integration varies a bit depending on cloud provider. we'll send the KMS integration matrix after the call.
[02:22] Samir Patel: great — also, data residency. Holloway processes eu resident data and we need audit logs forwarded to our splunk instance.
[02:36] Maya Chen: we can ship audit logs to an external syslog or S3 bucket — and per-route tracing can be configured. we'll add the logging flow to the security pack.
[02:52] Leo Grant: on the networking side, we have strict egress rules. would the marketplace deploy require opening egress to external endpoints for model downloads or health checks?
[03:10] Diego Alvarez: good question. for hosted installs we do pull model artifacts from Redwood's hosting by default, but for Private/on-prem we provide an air-gapped package and OCI images so that you can host all artifacts on your registry. there will be a short-setup step to pre-load the model files if you go fully air-gapped. sometimes that got transcribed as "air gap package" or "air-gap pack" in notes, little inconsistencies in speech.
[03:40] Ruth Ng: what's the difference between the private deploy and dedicated pools? we're trying to decide which route to list in the marketplace entry.
[03:53] Priya Nair: private deployment is customer-managed runtime; you run the runtime in your VPC/on-premises. Dedicated is our reserved managed GPU pools in Redwood infra. for marketplace listing, many customers list the private option as "bring your own" and also offer a managed offering behind a separate SKU.
[04:15] Samir Patel: ok that helps. for our pilot we want to deploy into our dev VPC first to validate latency and telemetry, then decide on production mode.
[04:26] Maya Chen: perfect. let's capture pilot success metrics now. what are your target p95 latency and throughput?
[04:33] Samir Patel: target p95 for shorter prompts (<=256 tokens) is 120ms, for long-form it's more flexible, maybe 600ms. throughput target is about 50 concurrent users with burst to 150.
[04:48] Diego Alvarez: quick note: those targets are aggressive for on-prem GPUs but achievable with batching and quantized models. we'll propose an instance sizing in the follow-up.
[04:59] Ruth Ng: does Redwood recommend quantized models for cost reasons and compatibility with our hardware? our current infra is T4 equivalent.
[05:12] Priya Nair: yes we will recommend quantization profiles. we'll include typical perf numbers; Diego will run a short benchmark with a T4/16GB baseline during the lab.
[05:28] Leo Grant: speaking of benchmarks, can we run a smoke benchmark during the pilot that measures p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens so we can compare to CloudWave?
[05:42] Maya Chen: yes that's part of the pilot spreadsheet — we'll add a CloudWave comparator row.
[05:50] [06:00] Speaker 6: (inaudible) -- sorry, I lost that --
[06:05] Asha Kapoor: one more security question — SSO, RBAC, and audit trails are must-haves. do you support SAML-based SSO and SCIM for group sync?
[06:18] Diego Alvarez: yes SAML and OIDC are supported; SCIM provisioning for users is supported in the private control plane. RBAC maps to roles and can integrate with your identity provider.
[06:31] Maya Chen: i'll put the SAML/SCIM integration guide in the notes, that will be in the security pack.
[06:39] Ruth Ng: another thing — the marketplace listing requires a quick start guide and a preflight checklist for compliance. do you have a sample we can reuse?
[06:50] Priya Nair: we do, we'll share a published quickstart that includes networking, KMS, and telemetry snippets.
[07:00] Samir Patel: about billing and meter — if we list a managed SKU, how does metering work for private installs? our legal team wants transparent usage billing for customers who consume via marketplace.
[07:15] Maya Chen: for marketplace-managed SKUs we surface metering hooks; for private deploys we recommend integrating our usage SDK or exporting token-level telemetry. we can co-author a metering adapter if needed.
[07:30] Leo Grant: will that require opening outbound ports for telemetry? our policy forbids most outbound traffic.
[07:38] Diego Alvarez: no, not necessarily. you can ship telemetry to a local collector and then push via a controlled egress, or we support a pull model where you export metrics to S3. we'll document options.
[07:52] Ruth Ng: great. on the topic of installer, can the helm chart be customized for our namespace and storage class?
[08:02] Diego Alvarez: yes values.yaml supports namespace, storageClass, resource overrides, and KV cache sizing. i'll prepare an example.
[08:12] Maya Chen: quick housekeeping — who owns the pilot timeline?
[08:17] Samir Patel: holloway will own provisioning in dev, redwood will provide the helm + deploy lab support.
[08:25] Maya Chen: ok i'll send a joint calendar invite for the lab week of May 11, diego you'll lead that.
[08:31] Diego Alvarez: yep will prepare labs: helm install, preloading model artifacts, KMS proof, and a short perf benchmark.
[08:40] [09:00] Ruth Ng: is there a preferred model variant for initial tests? we want a balanced quality/cost model.
[09:08] Priya Nair: recommend a mid-size quantized model, e.g., 7B q4; we'll list recommended variants in the follow-up with perf/cost ratios.
[09:20] Samir Patel: just flagging network encryption — we need mTLS between components, is that covered by default?
[09:28] Diego Alvarez: yes mTLS between runtime and gateway is supported, and can be provisioned via cert-manager in the helm chart. we'll include the example.
[09:39] Asha Kapoor: any SOC2 documentation you can share now?
[09:44] Maya Chen: i'll attach SOC2 and ISO certificates to the security pack, also a config for audit-forwarding to your SIEM.
[09:52] [10:10] Speaker 6: (whisper) how about fallback to hosted during capacity spikes?
[10:14] Maya Chen: good point, we can configure smart routing and fallback to Redwood hosted variants with policy-based routing — but that introduces data flow to hosted endpoints, which may violate residency. we discussed that tradeoff.
[10:29] Samir Patel: we want to avoid sending EU data out, so fallback isn't acceptable for production but could be ok in dev with scrubbed data.
[10:40] Diego Alvarez: noted. we can test fallback in dev with synthetic data.
[10:46] Maya Chen: all right let's recap next steps — maya to send security pack and listing checklist, diego to upload helm example and a perf test script, samir to share pilot metrics and dev VPC access. schedule lab week of May 11.
[11:05] Ruth Ng: and we'll fill the pilot spreadsheet with target thresholds and acceptance criteria.
[11:12] Maya Chen: perfect. any final questions?
[11:18] Samir Patel: none from me, thanks everyone.
[11:21] Maya Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links and the action items.

End of call.
